title: The Mandukya Upanishad
textType: Prose and verse scripture with commentary
dateDisplay: c. 1st century BCE–2nd century CE (date unsettled)
attributionNote: The shortest of the principal Upanishads, belonging to the Atharvaveda and transmitted without an author's name. GRETIL's e-text records the Māṇḍūkyamūlamantrabhāṣya, the commentary the tradition ascribes to Śaṅkara, and was input by members of the Sansknet project.
description: The Māṇḍūkya Upaniṣad is twelve verses on the syllable om and the four states of the self: the waking state, the dream, deep sleep, and the fourth, which is neither inward nor outward knowledge, beyond teaching and peace, the self to be realised. Its analysis of consciousness through the four quarters of om is the shortest complete statement of the Upanishadic teaching and the point from which Gauḍapāda's Kārikā and the whole Advaita literature on the Upanishads sets out.
historicalContext: Read in the Advaita schools as the crown of the Upanishads, the text is commented on in the Māṇḍūkya Kārikā attributed to Gauḍapāda and then in the commentary attributed to Śaṅkara; the three stand together in the school's teaching as scripture, verse and exposition.
availabilityNote: Complete: the twelve verses are streamed from GRETIL at read time, and the same file also carries the commentary attributed to Śaṅkara, which the reader shows beside the verses as a second pane. The Upanishad has a single chapter; the verses are indexed in reading order.
